title: Pub trivia score
topic: A friend averages two percentages from two halves of a trivia night
blurb: 75% plus 45% divided by 2 equals 60% — averaging percentages usually burns you.
prompt: A friend texted this walking out of pub trivia. Tap a line if the math is sloppy, or call it clean.

segments.label: The format
segments.text: Pub trivia had two 20-question halves tonight — music in the first half, geography in the second.

segments.label: The halves
segments.text: We nailed 75% in the music half and limped through 45% in geography.

segments.label: The total
segments.text: 75 plus 45 divided by 2 is 60, so we finished at 60% overall.

segments.label: The gripe
segments.text: Good enough for third place — missed the free nachos by one question.

conclusion: 75% in the first 20-question half and 45% in the second comes out to 60% overall.

diagnosis: Music and geography questions usually carry different point weights in trivia, so 20 questions each isn't equal.
Two halves of 20 is 40 questions, which isn't a clean base-100 total for adding percentages.
Splitting into two topics hides bonus questions that usually sit between halves.
Having 20 questions per half doesn't let you average percentages unless you got the same count right.
fix: Check whether geography questions were worth double points before combining halves.
Convert the 40 questions into raw points instead of working with percentages.
Include the halftime bonus question in the denominator before scoring.
Compare each half against the other teams separately instead of pooling them.

diagnosis: 75% and 45% come from two different categories, so you can't treat them on the same percentage scale.
45% of 20 isn't a whole number of questions, so the geography score has to be rounded.
75% of 20 is 14 questions and 45% is 8, so the raw numbers don't even match those percentages.
Quoting percentages instead of raw hits hides how many questions you actually missed.
fix: Convert to raw counts first: 14 in music and 8 in geography.
Check the geography score sheet since 45% of 20 rounds awkwardly.
Report 15 out of 20 and 9 out of 20 instead of percentages.
Keep the two categories separate since music is easier than geography.

diagnosis: You can't just average two percentages — adding 75% and 45% and dividing by 2 ignores how each half is weighted.
75% of 20 is 15 and 45% of 20 is 9; 24 out of 40 is 58%, not 60%.
When you combine two halves, the denominator doubles to 40, so you have to divide by 4, not 2.
Averaging 75% and 45% only works if you got the same number of wrong answers in both halves.
fix: Add the raw hits first (15 + 9 = 24) and weight by each half's difficulty.
Don't average percentages; report 75% on music and 45% on geography separately.
Use the weighted average formula instead of (75 + 45) / 2.

diagnosis: Missing by one question out of 40 is a 5% gap, which means second place had 65%, not 62.5%.
60% is 24 questions, and one more is 25 — you can't tell how close third place was without knowing total teams.
If you actually scored 58%, you were more than one question away from free nachos.
One question in a 20-question half is 5%, so missing by one question changes the overall average by 5 points.
fix: Check how many questions second place got — one question out of 40 is 2.5%, not 5%.
Re-check whether 25 out of 40 would have tied or beaten second place.
Fix the overall percentage first before blaming a single missed geography question.
Count total points including tiebreakers before saying it was one question.

clean_segments: Pub trivia had two 20-question halves tonight — music in the first half, geography in the second.
We nailed 75% in the music half and limped through 45% in geography.
75 plus 45 divided by 2 is 60, so we finished at 60% overall.
Good enough for third place — missed the free nachos by one question.
clean_conclusion: Averaging two percentages usually burns you — except both halves had the exact same 20 questions. 15 right plus 9 right out of 40 really is 60%.
